# New renderings chosen in iliad-137 (21.502–611)

| Greek | `l` | `i` | avoided on purpose |
|---|---|---|---|
| τὸν δ’ αὖτε προσέειπεν ἐϋστέφανος κελαδεινή (21.511, whole-line reply introduction; the speaker is Artemis, unnamed) | "Him then in turn addressed the fair-crowned, the resounding:" | "Then the fair-crowned, resounding one spoke to him in turn:" | "goddess" (adds a noun the Greek lacks), "answered" (reserved for ἠμείβετο), "loud-voiced"; built on the table's τὸν δ’ αὖτε προσέειπε pattern, the Odyssey's ἐϋστέφανος "fair-crowned" and the shipped κελαδεινή "the resounding" (16.183) |
| ἐϋστέφανος (21.511) | "fair-crowned" | "fair-crowned" | "well-garlanded", "crowned with flowers"; the Odyssey table's ἐυστέφανος (of Mycene), now also of a goddess |
| καμπύλα τόξα (21.502, plural, scattered) | "the bent bows" | "the bent bows" | "the bent bow" (the table's singular rendering of the plural form), "the bow and arrows" (adds); a departure from the table's "bow" for the plural because ἄλλυδις ἄλλα "some here, some there" needs more than one thing, and the note says so |
| ἀνῆκε (θεῶν δέ ἑ μῆνις ἀνῆκε, of smoke or a city, 21.523) | "has sent it up" | "has sent it up" | "has urged on" (kept for a person, the table's ἀνίημι "urge on", used at 21.545 Ἀγήνορα … ἀνῆκε), "has kindled", "has raised"; the object ἑ may be the smoke or the city, so "it" |
| ἀλείς (Ἀχιλῆα ἀλεὶς μένεν, 21.571) | "crouching" | "crouching" | "gathered himself", "drawn up"; follows the shipped ἧστο ἀλείς "sat crouched" (iliad-103) and the Odyssey's ἀλεὶς ὥς τ’ αἰετός |
| ἀσπάσιοι (of the Trojans reaching the city, 21.607) | "glad" | "glad to be there" | "welcome" (the Odyssey's ἀσπάσιος "a welcome sight", said of persons received by others), "gladly" (kept for the adverb ἀσπασίως) |
| πότμον ἐφέψεις (21.588, of the doom that will find Achilles) | "your doom will come upon" | "will meet your doom" | "will follow", "will pursue your fate" (the verb is ἐφέπω, not διώκω); follows the shipped πότμον ἐπίσπῃς "met your doom" (6.412) |
| ἀποέργαθε λαοῦ (21.599) | "kept away from the people" | "kept … away from the people" | "drove off", "led away" (adds motion toward a place), "shut out"; ἀπείργω "keep away from" |
| ξύλοχος (of a leopard's, 21.573) | "lair" | "lair" | "thicket", "covert"; follows the shipped βαθείης ἐκ ξυλόχοιο "out of the deep lair" (iliad-067) |
| ὑλαγμός (21.575) | "barking" | "barking" | "baying" (suggests hounds, which the Greek leaves unnamed), "yelping" |
| πυλαωρός (21.530) | "gatekeepers" | "gatekeepers" | "gate-guards", "watchers of the gates", "sentinels" |
| φάος τεύχω (πετασθεῖσαι τεῦξαν φάος, 21.538) | "made light" | "brought light" (+ note: φάος can also mean "relief, deliverance") | "let in the light" (adds a figure), "gave safety" |
| ἦ ῥα, καὶ ὀξὺν ἄκοντα … ἀφῆκε (21.590) | "He spoke, and the sharp javelin … let go" | "So he said, and let fly the sharp javelin" | keeps the table's ἦ ῥα καί "He spoke, and" / "So he said, and"; ἄκων "javelin" kept apart from ἔγχος "spear" |
